title: nOS entity — the base every organelle inherits
description:
The abstract nOS entity. It carries the harness every data node needs — compliance, access, cortex indexing, face rendering — as DATA, so a specific organelle inherits it by `allOf` instead of restating it. What may ACT on an entity is deliberately absent: `nos-cortex-lang.md` §2 and the Wing executor §2 both require that a capability must not be addable by data, so opcodes and handlers stay code, per runtime, hash-compared.

DIALECT: draft-07 with `definitions`, matching 6 of the 7 existing schemas in state/schema/. The estate already uses `$ref` 18 times — but every one is intra-file. Nothing here is a new idiom; this is the same factoring applied one level up, across a file boundary, which is the thing that has never been done.

EVIDENCE: the required core is not invented. All 72 plugin manifests declare name, version, description, type, requires and gdpr — measured, not assumed.

identity.description: Who this entity is. Empirically universal: 72/72 manifests carry all four.

name.description: Lower-kebab. Same charset as the agent-name rule in agent.schema.yaml, so one identifier style spans the estate.

kind.description: Which organelle this is. Open on purpose: the base must not need editing to admit a new kind.

taxonomy_anchor.description: Cortex node this entity hangs from, e.g. `tax:02.02.11`. Optional today; it is what makes `ent:` addressable from cortex-lang once the registry lands (cortex-self-core.md §6b).

compliance.description: GDPR Article 30 register row. ONE spelling — this supersedes the split between plugin.schema.json (5 required keys, `eu_residency`) and app.schema.json (7 required, `transfers_outside_eu`), which is the divergence `nos_gdpr.py` exists to paper over.

retention_days.description: Days. 0 = stores nothing itself (the horizon is owned by whatever it wires into). -1 = indefinite / no automatic horizon — 12 manifests use it and plugin.schema.json already allows it, so the genome does too. A schema that rejected live values would be a redesign wearing a schema's clothes.

eu_residency.description: CANONICAL residency field, and intended to become required. NOT required yet: 3 of 72 manifests (hermes-base, openclaw-base, vaultwarden-base) declare residency ONLY via the deprecated inverse `transfers_outside_eu: false`. That is a rename to make, not missing data — which is exactly the kind of distinction the split spelling was hiding. test_genome_contract.py pins the list so it can only shrink.

transfers_outside_eu.description: DEPRECATED alias — the logical inverse of eu_residency. Retained so the 22 manifests that carry it keep validating; consistency between the two is asserted by the validator, not expressible here. New entities declare eu_residency only.

access.description: Reachability and gating as ONE fact. Today this is split across five uncoordinated declarations — state/manifest.yml (a router exists), traefik_auth_modes (what attaches), traefik_skip_ids (whether to route), the plugin's authentik block (whether a provider exists to attach), and authentik_app_tiers (who may pass). Nothing compares them, and for `traefik` they disagreed: that is REM-144, a publicly reachable API whose only justification was a prose comment that had been false for three months.

routed.description: Whether an edge router is rendered for this entity at all.

gate.description: What stands in front of it. Mirrors the SSO trichotomy in CLAUDE.md plus the ungated case.

justification.description: Why an ungated route is acceptable. A FIELD, not a comment — the whole point of REM-144 is that a comment cannot be checked and rots silently.

tier.description: RBAC tier: 1 admin, 2 manager, 3 user, 4 guest.

then.description: A routed entity with no gate is anonymously reachable. It must say why, in a field a test can read. This clause IS the REM-144 gate, expressed as schema instead of as a hand-written pytest.

cortex.description: How the knowledge layer sees this entity.

indexed.description: Whether the entity is materialised as a cortex object (and therefore embedded, searchable, and visible in /explore).

body_fields.description: Which fields form the embedded body. Order is significant — it is what the router answers from.

excluded_fields.description: Fields that must never reach an embedding or an index. This is where the boolean the first draft wanted to bolt on actually belongs: as one facet field, scoped, rather than a loose column flag.

face.description: Render hints for the web desktop. Today these are scattered across hub_card, table defs and Wing columns, hand-mirrored between face and KEAP with no gate — and already drifted (face has 11 ColumnKinds to KEAP's 12).

entity.description: The base. An organelle composes this with `allOf` and adds its own kind-specific properties.
